# WS-12 layout decisions and inconsistencies

Companion to `docs/build/ws-12-deploy-and-infra.md` (2026-09-26). Section A lists every `[default chosen]` in the brief plus unmarked choices the brief had to make; Section B lists inconsistencies found in the plan, the SMP review, hosted-architecture, the Modal pipeline files and the sibling briefs (WS-00, WS-01, WS-03, WS-11, which landed while this brief was being written and to which module paths, workflow names and `make` targets were aligned). Nothing outside the brief and this file was edited.

Sources actually read for the values: SMP module sources as copied into `huntertcarver/chatgraph` (`shared-assets/delivery/terraform-governance-pack/modules/*`, `shared-assets/delivery/terraform-root-stack-starter/*`, `shared-assets/security/secret-handoff-baseline/*`, `shared-assets/runtime/cloud-run-baseline-template/*`, `shared-assets/eventing/pubsub-contracts/*`, `shared-assets/observability/*`; the SMP repo itself returned 404 for this agent's token), chatgraph's `infra/chatgraph-prod-bootstrap/main.tf` and `.github/workflows/flagship-delivery-prod.yaml` (state in `smp-substrate-tfstate-prod`, own WIF pool, `objectAdmin` grant), `internal/modal-pipeline/{app.py,bench.py,README.md,benchmark.md,runs/*}`, Modal docs (OIDC claims, `modal deploy --tag/--strategy`, `modal app rollback/rollover/history`, `modal environment`, budgets, `Image.from_dockerfile`/`uv_sync`), Terraform registry (`google_cloud_run_v2_service/job` GPU fields), and `docs/build/ws-{00,01,03,11}-*.md`.

## A. Decisions

| # | Decision | Where | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Three PRs (A Modal, B Terraform+CI, S in the SMP repo) instead of one | §0 | A does not depend on WS-01's modules or on GCP; B does; S lives in another repo with its own CI. |
| 2 | GitHub `prod` environment: deployment branches `main` only, required reviewer Hunter | §3, §4.9 (SMP exception 6) | Human gate for `apply=true` and prod deploys without code; `DLV-DEC-005` (no manual prod approval) recorded as an exception. Also gates prod `infra.yml` plans. |
| 3 | Deployed Modal app name `house-scanning`; WS-01's `hss-capture-api` is `include`d, WS-03's functions register on the same `app`; volume stays `house-capture-pipeline` | §3, §4.1.1 | Plan says one app; WS-01 §4.19 says "WS-12 composes `app.include(api_app)` in `server/modal_app.py`"; WS-03 builds on WS-00's `app`. URL keeps WS-01's label: `https://huntertcarver-<env>--capture-api.modal.run`. |
| 4 | Deploy-time selector is `SMP_ENVIRONMENT` (not a new `HSS_ENV`) | §3, §4.5 | WS-01 `modal_entry.py` and WS-03's deploy line already read `SMP_ENVIRONMENT` at deploy time. |
| 5 | GPU `Dockerfile` carries no application code; Modal adds `server/` with `add_local_python_source`; Python 3.12 via `uv python install` | §4.1.2 | Code changes never rebuild the 10-min image; WS-00 fixed py312 repo-wide and expects WS-12 to confirm the image. |

| 7 | `KNOBS` (`HSS_PIPELINE_GPU`, `HSS_PIPELINE_MIN_CONTAINERS` 0 / 1 in demo window, `HSS_PIPELINE_MAX_CONTAINERS` 3 dev / 6 prod) exposed from `server/modal_app.py` for WS-03's `Pipeline` decorator; timeout 1200 s and `scaledown_window` 900 s are WS-03's; API `min_containers=1`, `max_containers=1` are WS-01's | §4.1.6 | The class is WS-03's file; WS-12 must not edit it, so the knobs are an import. |

Supersedes this brief's first draft (one pool, `create_pool`). |

## B. Inconsistencies found (report only; no doc edited)

1. **Modal WIF recipe in `docs/smp-adoption-review.md` §4.2 cannot work as written.** `google.subject = assertion.sub` exceeds GCP's 127-byte limit for Modal's `sub` claim, and providers `modal-<env>` would share issuer `https://oidc.modal.com` inside one pool. WS-01's module (pool per environment, short subject) fixes both; the brief follows WS-01.
2. **Review §4.2 vs §4.3:** service accounts `hss-gha-<env>` per environment, but `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL` is listed as a repo-level variable. Resolved with one SA (A.12). WS-01 §1.4 says "CI reuses SMP's GitHub WIF pool **and GitHub SA**": the pool is shared, the SA is not (SMP's substrate SA carries `roles/viewer` and IAM-admin roles); the brief keeps a dedicated `hss-gha` in `house-scanning` per Hunter's "narrowed roles".
3. **Review §4.3 and `internal/modal-pipeline/README.md` say the bench stops at $160;** `bench.py` has `SPEND_STOP_USD = 40.0` (README stale; the brief cites $40).
4. **Plan §1 and `benchmark.md` say the GPU is blocked on a Modal payment method;** `runs/bench-l4.jsonl` and `billing.json` (2026-09-26 21:3x UTC) show L4 containers running. The current blocker is the pycolmap 3.11.1 API (`Database.open`, `Image.data_id`, `IncrementalPipelineOptions.use_prior_position/random_seed`), already WS-04's start-gate item 4. No house timing exists yet.
5. **Plan §6 WS-12 and hosted-architecture §1 row 10 list a "GCS signer key" Modal secret;** the review, WS-01 and this brief are keyless (WIF + `signBlob`). Plan and hosted-architecture also name Sentry for prod; the review defers it (`OBS-DEC-009`).
6. **Bucket naming:** hosted-architecture §2.2 example uses `base-capture-prod`; the review and WS-01 use `hss-captures-<env>`; SMP's convention (`${product_id}-${environment}-<surface>`, adopted for labels and env vars) would give `house-scanning-<env>-captures`. The brief keeps `hss-`; Hunter may want one convention.
7. **Review §4.2 omits `project_name`,** a required variable of `gcp_project_env_baseline` (no default). Brief passes `project_name = var.project_id`.
8. **Review §4.2 bootstrap order** (local state, then `init -migrate-state`) is only needed on the fallback path; with the shared bucket Hunter's identity can `init` against GCS from the first apply.
9. **Review §4.1 gives the `fixtures` CI job to WS-12 (§4.3 "ci.yml (extend)")** while WS-00 owns `ci.yml` jobs `contracts`, `fixtures` and WS-11 owns `gates-offline`. Brief adds only `terraform`, `modal-check`, `workflows-lint`.
10. **Review §3 "Override `workload_identity_provider_id`"** implies a new provider in an existing pool; the module hard-codes one repository and same-issuer duplicates are a risk, so the SMP module needs the small `additional_attribute_conditions` extension (PR S item 1).
11. **State key conventions coexist in `smp-substrate-tfstate-prod`:** chatgraph uses `products/chatgraph/prod` (scaffold renderer), `backend-conventions.yaml` says `<product>/<environment>`; Hunter's `house-scanning/<env>` follows the convention. No action, but the bucket now holds both patterns.
12. **`internal/modal-pipeline/app.py` builds Python 3.11** (`add_python="3.11"`) while the repo is 3.12 (WS-00 §12 expects `add_python="3.12"`). The brief installs 3.12 in the Dockerfile; the builder must confirm a `pycolmap==3.11.1` cp312 wheel exists, else fall back to 3.11 for the GPU image only and note it.
13. **hosted-architecture §2.2 base URL `https://capture-api.<domain>/v1`** needs a custom domain (Modal Team plan); the demo uses `*.modal.run` URLs (`https://huntertcarver-<env>--capture-api.modal.run`).
14. **Plan §6 WS-12 "One Modal app: `capture-api` (asgi), `early_*` functions, `Pipeline`" vs the sibling briefs:** WS-01 ships `api_app = modal.App("hss-capture-api")` (to be `include`d), WS-03 ports `Pipeline` into `server/orchestrator/modal_functions.py`, WS-00 creates the `server/modal_app.py` stub. The plan's one-app intent survives only through WS-12's composition module and WS-03 importing `app` from `server.modal_app`; the brief pins that rule.
15. **Plan §6 WS-12 done-when "cost report per house printed"** presumes successful pipeline runs; none exist until WS-04's pycolmap port lands, so the brief accepts a cost report over `ok:false` records with a stated caveat.
16. **WS-00 §12 default `gs://hss-fixtures-<env>`** vs this brief's single `gs://hss-fixtures` (A.22); WS-00's `fetch_fixtures.py` has `--only small|large|all` but no per-item filter, so deploy verify fetches ≈ 370 MB to get one 37 MB tar (ask recorded in the brief §12 Q5).
17. **WS-00 vs WS-01 fixture layout:** WS-00 §6 caches tars at `.fixtures/packets/<house>.tar`; WS-01 §1.2/§6 expects extracted folders `.fixtures/packets/eth3d-electro/packet.arkit-nonlidar.json`; WS-11's replay takes the tar. The brief uses the tar (WS-11). WS-00/WS-01 should agree on who extracts.
18. **WS-01 §12 expects "WS-12's `deploy.yml` redeploys `dev`/`prod` at least daily"** for the static Modal identity token; the brief provides `rollover.yml` (`modal app rollover`, daily) instead of a daily redeploy, which needs no code change and keeps the pinned SHA.
19. **WS-11 §4.12 `e2e.yml` runs `make fixtures ONLY=all` from a `gs://` mirror without GCP auth;** the mirror is private, so the workflow needs `permissions: id-token: write` and WS-12's `auth-gcp-oidc` step (ask recorded in the brief §4.5/§12 Q6). WS-01's interim replay uses `--token-env`, WS-11's final CLI `--token`.
20. **WS-03 §4.1 `Pipeline.timeout` 1200 s vs app.py `50*60`;** the brief adopts WS-03's 1200 (its coordinator runs 1560 s, the plan's hard stop is 20 min). WS-03's `Pipeline` decorator hard-codes `gpu="L4"` and containers; the brief asks WS-03 to read `server.modal_app.KNOBS` (§12 Q6).

## C. Builder additions (WS-12, 2026-09-26)

Recorded by the builder. Sections A and B above were not rewritten.

| # | Decision | Where | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | One draft PR on `ws-12/infra-terraform` holds both the Modal composition and the Terraform stack, plus the SMP diff | Mac rule: one worktree `~/hss-wt/ws-12` | The card lists `ws-12/deploy-modal` and `ws-12/infra-terraform`. The Mac rule allows one worktree and one draft. Split later if the integrator wants the card's two PRs. |
| B2 | `module.capture_bucket` and `module.modal_wif` are not called | `main.tf` `TODO(ws-01)` | Those modules are not on `main`. Outputs that would come from them are null. |
| B3 | Runtime SA `objectViewer` bindings on `hss-fixtures` are comments, not resources | `fixtures.tf` | The service accounts do not exist until WS-01. Binding a missing member fails the first apply. `hss-gha` can read the bucket through `roles/storage.admin`. |
| B4 | `github_wif_pool_name` cross-check is a `check` block, not a `validation` block | `locals.tf` | Terraform 1.8 allows a variable validation to read only that variable. `~> 7.28` allows 7.46, so the provider constraint is `~> 7.28.0` and the lock is 7.28.0. |
| B5 | `modal` is a dev dependency (`modal==1.5.5`) | `pyproject.toml` | Mac rule. The GPU image uses `--no-dev`; Modal injects its client. `modal-check` syncs the dev group. |
| B6 | GPU extra does not downgrade numpy, opencv, pillow, or scipy | lock | Those pins are already on `main` (numpy 2.5.3, opencv 5.0.0.93, pillow 12.3.0, scipy 1.18.1, pycolmap 4.2.0). Torch 2.5.1 and torchvision 0.20.1 come from the cu124 index. |
| B7 | Model tarballs are `uv pip install` lines in the Dockerfile, not lock entries | `Dockerfile` | Unnamed sdists. Torch is re-pinned from cu124 after those installs. |
| B8 | `CPU_IMAGE` calls `uv_sync()` with no `extras=["api"]` | `server/modal_app.py` | The `api` extra is WS-01's and is not in `pyproject.toml`. |
| B9 | `api_app` and `server.orchestrator.modal_functions` are imported only if present | `server/modal_app.py` | WS-01 and WS-03 are not on `main`. The app is `smoke_cpu` until they land. |
| B10 | COLMAP git tag `4.2.0` | `Dockerfile` | GitHub release `4.2.0` exists and matches `pycolmap==4.2.0`. The image was not built: the Docker daemon was down. |
| B11 | SMP auth action copied verbatim (no `setup-gcloud`) | `.github/actions/auth-gcp-oidc` | `38b696f` has only `google-github-actions/auth@v2`. `deploy.yml` adds `setup-gcloud` as the next step. |
| B12 | Fixtures bucket IAM for runtime SAs waits | see B3 | Same as B3. |
